title: Team ICB on FloorSet-Prime: all 100 test designs at the ground truth's cost
subtitle: 10/21-10/24/2026  |  all 100 test designs  |  updated 10/24
summary: Where the numbers come from. The 10/23 result (best of six flows per design, picked without the ground truth, then a 60 s polish by the pair re-cut refinement; the reinforcement-learning tree builder's flow gives 59 of its 100 layouts) went through one more stage on 10/24: repair moves for the soft violations left (an edge-pinned block that could not reach its edge, split clusters), then a large-neighbourhood search (LNS) for wirelength. Both re-run the partitioner on a window of the layout. 17 designs changed since the 10/23 report (77 and 98 first by the corridor move on the evening of 10/23, see below); the other 83 were already at 1.000 and are unchanged.

Read the 1.000s with two caveats. The cost is floored at 1.000, so these designs match or beat the ground truth; on wirelength the closest five are only 0.05-0.2% below it. And the search time was steered with the ground truth: LNS ran in rounds, and a design left the queue once its contest cost reached 1.000. Every decision to keep a layout used only our own measures (wirelength and violation counts, no ground truth), but a contest run would have to stop on its own rule. This stage cost about 16 CPU-hours, 10 of them on design 76; the mean recorded run time per design went from 373 s to 749 s. Run time was not the focus, and there is much to do there.

p: The partition flow's annealer (slicing tree over the soft blocks, rigid blocks placed in corners, cuts that wrap around preplaced blocks) can also run on part of a layout: the union of the blocks a window touches is the region, and all other blocks stay put as fixed context for wirelength and violations. Four moves are built on it; each keeps its result only if our score (wirelength against the starting layout and soft violations) drops.

Window re-partition for an edge pin (design 80, 1.054). Block 81, a long strip, had to touch the bottom edge 94 units away, through a band of blocks no pair move could cross. The window spans the strip from the block to its edge, widened in steps; a small search-only penalty on the block's distance to its edge steers the annealer. Valid with the pin met, then LNS: 1.000.

Pocket swap (design 50, 1.057). Block 9 must touch the top-right corner, which lies in a pocket walled off by two preplaced blocks and the frame, filled exactly by two other blocks. No re-shaping can reach it: the pocket has to be refilled. Its area (534) is block 9 (406) plus 128, matched within the 1% area tolerance only by a block of the MIB pair 5/6 (132). The move fills the pocket with block 9 plus such a partner, and re-partitions a window of the main region so the two displaced blocks (one with a top-edge pin of its own) take the space it left: 1.000. Only one of about 35 annealing runs found a valid layout with every pin met, so this move is hit and miss.

Cluster shift (design 8, 1.028). Its zero-white-space layout scored 1.125 on one split cluster: a rigid MIB pair sat 22 units below its preplaced cluster mate, and one of the pair is pinned to the right edge, so it fits in one spot only. Moving the pair as a unit until it touches its mate, fixing it there and re-partitioning the window around both places gives 1.000 (wirelength 16% below the ground truth). A window search with a penalty on the split alone never found it (the annealer kept trading the split for the edge pin).

LNS for wirelength (14 designs). A random block, a window grown around it to 6-20 blocks, 3 s of annealing, a greedy descent, and the result kept only if the score drops; repeated until the time is up (3.4% of the 10,691 windows tried won, more early on, fewer late). One 900 s run took design 97 from 1.012 to 1.000; 13 more designs followed in rounds of 900-2,400 s, several seeds in parallel. On design 76 the packer layout picked on 10/23 (1.041) has 5.6% white space that LNS cannot remove; started instead from its zero-white-space partition layout (1.047, one split cluster), LNS rejoined the cluster and then cut wirelength over six rounds to 0.1% below the ground truth.

Corridor re-slice (10/23 evening; designs 77 and 98). An edge-pinned block and a chain of soft blocks between it and its edge (or the band of blocks in that strip) are merged and re-cut by random slicing trees with the block on the edge side; the best few get a greedy descent. It fixed 77 (1.041 to 1.000) and 98 (1.029 to 1.002), but not 50 and 80, which needed the moves above.

Reproduction: scripts/reproduce_final.sh now ends with this stage (scripts/lns_final.py, about 5 h more): per design it starts from both the polished pick and the best zero-white-space flow layout, repairs violations, runs LNS rounds, and keeps the cheapest on the contest formula relative to the polished pick (no ground truth). It uses the same stop-at-1.000 time allocation as above. LNS is timed and random, so a rerun lands near these numbers, not on them; the full rebuild has not been run yet.

Prime's ground truth tiles its frame exactly (zero white space) with rectilinear blocks, and 85 of the 100 test layouts cannot be built from straight cuts alone. The plan agreed on 10/21 combines two published rectilinear floorplanners with reinforcement learning (RL), inside a mix of methods whose best layout is picked per design:
1. Global floorplan in the style of RPolyPlan (arXiv 2610.28276): an augmented-Lagrangian optimization of soft-block boxes with pairwise overlap sharing, inside the exact frame.
2. Legalization in the style of JigsawPlanner (ICCAD 2024): Prime's coordinates and areas are integers, so unit grid cells can give every block its exact area with no white space and no overlap.
3. Clean-up moves that keep areas exact, chosen by an RL policy instead of hand-written rules.
Alongside: (A) an RL policy that builds the slicing tree for the existing zero-white-space partition flow.

sections.h: What was built overnight, and what worked (history)
p: Regression fix. A cache cap added on 10/21 to share the machine with Vivado made the partition search clear its cache constantly; big designs failed or lost 0.3-0.6. The old size is the default again (about 6 GB for 6 workers), and the full partition run was redone with it ('Partition' column).

Stages 1-2 (grid flow, prime_grid.py). The augmented-Lagrangian global floorplan and the exact grid assignment (a transportation linear program solved with HiGHS) both work end to end, and their wirelength is good (about 6% over the ground truth). But stage 1 does not converge at 0% white space, the cell assignment leaves staircase edges that break the 16-corner cap, and clusters split, so few layouts came out valid. This flow is parked; its parts are reusable.

Stage 3 on the partition flow (rl/refine.py) -- the night's main gain. Instead of legalizing a grid, the stage-3 moves were applied to the partition flow's already-valid layouts: two touching soft blocks are merged and re-split by one straight cut at the exact area of each; a rigid block and a soft neighbour swap places within their joint region; three soft blocks are re-split by two cuts. Areas stay exact and white space stays zero. A move is kept if it lowers a stand-in for the contest cost (wirelength and soft violations). Pairs are re-cut independently of the tree, so layouts leave the slicing family. Greedy descent is followed by iterated local search: a few random re-cuts ('kicks'), descend again, keep only improvements.

RL in stage 3 (rl/kick_policy.py). A small network scores candidate re-cuts from local features (immediate gain, distance of each block from where its nets pull it, net weight between the pair, soft violations) and samples the kicks of the iterated local search; REINFORCE, comparing several kicks from the same state. v1 (111 training designs, re-scoring every candidate after each move) tied with random kicks on 5 held-out designs; v2 (one scoring pass over 60 sampled pairs per kick, trained from a pool of 150 training layouts) lost on 14 of 19 held-out designs (mean 1.018 vs 1.011 for random kicks at equal time). Random kicks stay in use.

RL tree builder (A, rl/tree_policy.py). The partition annealer used to start from a tree that is invalid on most large designs (41-51 bad leaves on test designs 60 and 90), mostly because rigid blocks ended up as siblings. The policy builds the tree top-down over the real region, masks splits that leave a rigid-only subtree or a bad leaf, and learns sort keys, cut directions and split points by REINFORCE against the mean of 8 sampled trees per design (best validation tree cost 8.56, against 21.7 for the old first tree). Each restart starts its search from the best of 32 sampled trees. Its first A/B looked like a loss (2 of 12 layouts invalid), but both failures came from the refiner's polygon output (1e-6 coordinate jogs, a collinear vertex), fixed on 10/22 together with a guard that checks every refined layout. A first full run then crashed on 17 designs from a refiner sliver bug, and the crash also switched the restarts to serial; both were fixed and those designs rerun.

Refiner output: coordinates closer than 1e-5 are merged (rigid blocks keep their exact values), collinear vertices removed, cuts leaving pieces thinner than 0.001 rejected; every refined layout is checked against the evaluator's hard rules, with the unrefined one as fallback.

Evaluator shape check (rl/polygon.py canonical_key): float noise from a fractional position left a duplicate vertex, so an exact fixed shape read as different; the ground truth still scores 1.000 on all 100 designs.
A crashing restart made the restart pool fall back to serial for the rest of the run (4x slower); restarts now catch their own errors.

Targeted pushes for edge-pin misses and split clusters (rl/refine.py fix_violations): fixed designs 66 and 70 (to 1.000); blocks walled in by preplaced or rigid blocks (designs 50, 80, 81, 93, 98) still miss their edge.

Design 75 (1.289 -> 1.003): a 5 x 7 pocket walled in by preplaced blocks could only be filled by a member of a soft MIB group of area 35, but MIB groups got a fixed 1.5-aspect rectangle that never fit. A rectangular pocket now gives a matching MIB group its shape (rl/partition.py _fill_pockets).

Design 77 (1.157 -> 1.041): the solve-time pick (prime_evaluate.relative_cost, and rl/repack.py contest_relative_cost) added ratios where the contest adds gaps; the base near 2 doubled the weight of soft violations and chose the packer layout over a better partition one. With gaps the pick equals picking with the ground truth (1.010 both). The original Lite contest repo has the same function and was not changed.

Edge pins and clusters behind walls: a beam-search 'route push' lets a block go around preplaced or rigid blocks (it fixed the split cluster of design 81, 1.044 -> 1.005); designs 50, 77, 80 and 98 have no valid sequence of pair moves to their edge and need a new move (e.g. swapping with a block already on the edge). A shape check now rejects moves that leave a self-touching ring (design 80).
Grid flow: starting stage 1 with 10% slack and shrinking it to zero does not help; it stalls at the same violation, so its formulation needs rework.

RL tree builder with a reward closer to its use (cost after a short anneal from each sampled tree, 6 designs in parallel): no gain on unseen designs. Round 1 (1.5 s timed anneals) lost a fair paired test, worse on 18 of 30 held-out designs; the timed anneal made the reward follow machine load. Round 2 (3,000-step deterministic anneals) improved its 30 validation designs (cost ratio to the seed tree 1.003 -> 0.889) but tied the current policy on 30 fresh held-out designs (15 better, 15 worse; mean 3.514 vs 3.458): the checkpoint choice fitted the validation set. The 10/21 policy stays in use. A real gain likely needs far more updates than the 101-355 a 1.5-hour run allows.

table_note: Quality cost per design (the contest cost without its runtime term). 1.000 is the ground truth's own score and also the floor: gaps below zero count as zero, so a design at 1.000 matches or beats the ground truth. 'HPWL gap' is the best layout's wirelength relative to the ground truth (negative = shorter). 'Picked' is the flow the best-of chose without looking at the ground truth.
anchor_note: The five anchor designs (0, 24, 49, 74 and 98, spread over the size range) drawn at one scale: the ground truth, the partition flow before refinement, and the final layout (green frame).

p: 1. Run the full rebuild (scripts/reproduce_final.sh, about 21 h) to confirm the 10/24 stage reaches these numbers without hand-run rounds.
2. A stopping rule without the ground truth for the LNS stage (e.g. stop a design when a round improves it by less than a set amount), and the score that gives.
3. More margin where wirelength is within 0.2% of the ground truth (designs 77, 97, 76, 81, 36).
4. RL: learn which window to re-partition (most LNS windows lose), in place of the random choice; training data comes free from every LNS run.
5. The grid flow (stages 1-2) still needs its global floorplan reformulated to converge at zero white space.
6. The pick-rule fix ported to the Lite contest repo still needs a full Lite evaluation (about 6 h).
7. Run time: every stage is anytime; the contest budget decides how long each runs.
